meta.title: Yoruba Phrases and Expressions
meta.subtitle: 123 phrases, proverbs and sentences · both directions
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Yoruba → English and English → Yoruba, each a card of its own with its own schedule. 123 phrases and sentences in five parts: 26 greetings and wishes (Yoruba greets by the time of day and by what someone is doing — kúuṣẹ́ to someone at work, kúùjókòó to someone sitting), 22 everyday phrases and exclamations, 29 idioms and similes ('as sweet as honey'), 16 proverbs, each with its meaning and its literal reading, and 30 short sentences. Not a level: it follows the Yoruba A1, A2 and B1 decks and teaches none of their words again. WHERE THESE COME FROM: the phrases, idioms and proverbs are English Wiktionary's own entries, with its meanings and, where it gives one, its literal reading — none is written or translated by Folio — and 14 have Wiktionary's usage example; the sentences are Tatoeba's, at most nine words, printed as Tatoeba has them, each with its number. Both sources are small for Yoruba: Wiktionary has 17 Yoruba proverbs and Tatoeba about 60 translated sentences, so this deck is short. Left out: dialect greetings (Ekiti, Ìjẹ̀bú), the ritual formulas of the Ifá and Ògbóni societies, entries Wiktionary marks offensive, and sentences written without their tone marks or misspelt. There is no speaker button: few devices have a Yoruba voice. Sources: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0); Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
